prompt.alinti: Browsing the web is slow for computers. Most programs that browse websites for you are actually just heavy versions of the same web browsers you use on your desktop every day. They're bulky, they eat up your computer's memory, and they're honestly overkill if you just want to grab information from a page. That's why this new project, called LightPanda, has grabbed 34,926 stars on GitHub. It's a completely new way to browse, written from scratch to be incredibly lightweight and fast. Imagine trying to drive a giant, heavy tour bus just to pick up a single envelope from the post office. That's basically what other tools are doing. LightPanda is like a nimble, high-speed motorcycle that gets in and out of the web in seconds. It's built for tasks where a computer agent needs to visit hundreds of pages, fill out forms, or pull data without slowing down your entire system. You can even talk to it in plain English to tell it exactly where you're going. You can tell it where to go and what to click. It's basically a robot assistant that understands how to use the internet just like a person would, but with way less effort.
